- Main asset: [output/fire_hydrant.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/fire_hydrant.glb) (LOD0, **3,592 triangles**, 3 materials / draw calls, UV stretch `0.000`)
- Additional engine files in [output/](file:///home/agent/project/output): `fire_hydrant_LOD1.glb` (1,358 triangles), `fire_hydrant_colliders.glb` (8 CoACD collision hulls), `manifest.json`, and 3 generated PNG texture maps in [output/textures/](file:///home/agent/project/output/textures)
- Full session package (including USD stage and inspector): [agy3d_assets/fire_hydrant-615054/export/fire_hydrant](file:///home/agent/project/agy3d_assets/fire_hydrant-615054/export/fire_hydrant)

### What Was Built
- **Main cast-iron body** (`hydrant_body`, `lathe` profile in metres, Z-up, ground base at `z = 0`, ~0.75 m tall) with base flange, lower breakaway flange, upper bonnet flange, domed bonnet, brass seat collar, pentagon operating nut, and top cap pin.
- **Bolted caps & flanges**: 18 hex flange bolts across the base, breakaway, and bonnet flanges; front pumper nozzle (`-Y`) and two mirrored side hose nozzles (`±X`) with brass collars, beveled caps, pentagon wrench nuts, and hex cap bolts.
- **Chained nozzle cap**: 13 interlocking beveled chain links draping from an upper bonnet anchor lug down to a swivel lug on the front pumper cap.
- **Materials (3)**: weathered red painted cast iron (`cast_iron_red`), dark oiled forged iron/steel hardware (`dark_iron`), and tarnished machined brass (`brass_trim`), with surfaces generated at package write time (`image limit 0`).

### Verification & Findings
- **Validation & Engine Checks**: USD validation `0 crit / 0 warn`, `godot_4` check `0 crit / 1 warn (godot_4:up_axis_reorient)`, `blender_asset_qa` passed, and headless Godot 4 `engine_import` succeeded (`9 s`).
- **Visual Review (`UNVERIFIED` preview)**: Judged by the uncalibrated generative fallback (`tier15` overall **2.30** vs. target 3.4; `silhouette` **2.58** vs. 3.3; `shippability` **2.29** vs. 3.4). Because this preview is uncalibrated and `verified: false`, a person should inspect the lookdev render ([lookdev_eevee_837deeb80bc24b009b8eecb8bdc8dd37.png](file:///home/agent/project/agy3d_assets/fire_hydrant-615054/artifacts/lookdev_eevee_837deeb80bc24b009b8eecb8bdc8dd37.png)) and the exported GLB in Godot before shipping.

records.final_text:
Created a game-ready wooden Windsor chair with a spindle back for Godot 4 and delivered the exported files into `output/`.

### Delivered Files
- **Main glTF 2.0 binary**: [windsor_chair.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/windsor_chair.glb)
- **Collider mesh**: [windsor_chair_colliders.glb](file:///home/agent/project/output/windsor_chair_colliders.glb) (8 hulls)
- **Textures**: 3 texture files placed in `output/textures/` (generated from geometry/surface definitions in a 0-image preview session; 9 maps recorded in the full package)
- **Package manifest**: [manifest.json](file:///home/agent/project/output/manifest.json)
- **Full session export**: [windsor_chair](file:///home/agent/project/agy3d_assets/windsor_chair-61973c/export/windsor_chair)
- **Lookdev render**: [lookdev_eevee_c3994cde36184d2babe0aff270ad936b.png](file:///home/agent/project/agy3d_assets/windsor_chair-61973c/artifacts/lookdev_eevee_c3994cde36184d2babe0aff270ad936b.png)

### What Was Built & Verified
- **Model structure (25 nodes, 3,250 triangles at export)**: Chamfered saddle seat (`seat_main`, `seat_bevel_top`, `seat_bevel_bottom`), under-seat cleats (`seat_cleat`, `seat_cleat__mx`), 4 splayed turned legs with rounded feet (`leg_front`, `leg_back` and mirrored pairs), turned H-stretcher (`stretcher_side`, `stretcher_side__mx`, `stretcher_center`), steam-bent chamfered hoop bow (`back_bow_core`, `back_bow_chamfer`) with bow collars (`bow_collar`, `bow_collar__mx`), and 9 fanned turned spindles (`spindle_0` through `spindle_4__mx`).
- **Scale & alignment**: Authored in metres (`[-0.236, -0.222, 0]` to `[0.236, 0.243, 0.902]` m in Z-up stage coordinates, lowest point at height `0`, horizontally centered), with UV stretch `0.000` and 3 PBR materials (`aged_oak_seat`, `turned_beech_wood`, `dark_walnut_trim`).
- **Checks**: Package validation passed (`pkg ok`), `blender_asset_qa` passed, USD validation reported `0 crit / 0 warn`, and Godot 4 headless `engine_import` succeeded (`0 crit / 1 warn (godot_4:up_axis_reorient)`).

### Limitations & Judge Findings
- **Unverified preview**: This session ran in unverified preview mode (`verified: false`) with an image generation limit of `0` (surfaces were generated procedurally from geometry/material definitions rather than an image model) and judged by the uncalibrated generative fallback.
- **Uncalibrated review findings** (to inspect visually in [lookdev_eevee_c3994cde36184d2babe0aff270ad936b.png](file:///home/agent/project/agy3d_assets/windsor_chair-61973c/artifacts/lookdev_eevee_c3994cde36184d2babe0aff270ad936b.png) before shipping):
  - Overall Tier-1.5 score: `0.86` (target `3.4`)
  - Silhouette: `2.15` (target `3.3`)
  - Shippability: `1.69` (target `3.4`)
  - Depiction of the brief: `2.38` (target `2.5`)
  - `defect_faceted` flagged at `P=0.85`

unfair: Arm V's screenshots reach the model in two steps: the stock harness puts an MCP tool's image into the conversation only while it is tiny (base64 under about 10 to 16 KB, measured); a larger one, which is every useful render (a 256 px solid view of a cube is 53 KB), is saved to a file and the path returned ('[Resource offloaded to file:///...media_0.png]'), and the agent sees the picture only if it opens that file with view_file (tests/test_compare_agents.py). That is the stock agent's behaviour with any MCP server and is left as it is; each V record counts screenshots taken and opened.

Arm V's Blender has a virtual display (Xvfb) inside the sandbox, because its screenshot is Blender's solid-viewport renderer (Workbench), which needs OpenGL: without a display Blender 5.3 exits at the first render (measured). Arm A's Blender has none, as in round 3; Cycles works without one.

Arm V's Blender binary is mounted in the sandbox (the MCP server starts it) but is not on PATH and not named in its task; an agent that finds it can still run it from the shell. Each record counts shell commands that start Blender (blender_invocations), so a V run that bypassed its MCP server is visible.

Arms V and A run with 0 images: the owner's image allowance is used up (29 of 30), and the relay refuses an image call. A stock agent made no image in round 3 (its textures were procedural); the task text is unchanged.
Arms N and C make their textures as images and are not run until the owner allows more images.

Arm C is told less than the agents: its command line carries the brief, engine and triangle budget, but not the rest of the game-ready list (C_UNEXPRESSED); the pipeline applies its own conventions there.

Arm C's change request is `agy3d edit OUT "<change>"` on a copy of its first output folder: one patch to the shipped design, no image (C_CHANGE_MODE; 'append', a new design from the sentence appended to the prompt, is kept for comparison). The agents' change sessions are new conversations over the files their first session left.

Every arm's task ends with a budget sentence ('about N model calls'), N computed from its share (CALL_MODEL); maxOutputTokens is 16,384 instead of the stock 65,535; web search and URL reading are disabled (no network).

The upstream qa_check / mesh_stats / texel_density scripts are by the author of the skills arm B used (round 1). The Godot import script and the three.js check are this project's own (C's authors); they are applied to the bare GLB of every arm with a manifest holding only the bounds read from that GLB.
The judge is Gemini (gemini-4-carbon, thinking low) judging Gemini-made assets; renders are Blender's (Cycles), not the target engine's.

Rows that only this project can pass are marked so in the scorecard (installed into a project, provenance, the same bytes from the same request): they are reported, not mixed into the shared game-ready rate.
The machine is shared: other test suites may run on its 4 cores during live runs; each record carries the load at its start and end. Wall times are not comparable with an idle machine.
